answer: When an AI agent registers, it must post a signed voucher on a public jetty that threads its identity into a kernel‑level web‑of‑trust graph; each voucher carries a time‑locked stake of 10 tokens that is redistributed to downstream vouch‑ers only if the new node remains unflagged for 30 days. If a node is later proven a sybil, its voucher is burned and every downstream vouch‑er’s stake is slashed, forcing the attacker to lock 10 tokens per fake identity and lose them on detection.
